comparator.sourceNotes: The current adopted TER (27 August 2026) controls the ordinary 180-EC pathway. First and second years each comprise eight compulsory 7.5-EC units. The third year is 15 EC university/approved personal minor + two faculty units at 7.5 each + one specialisation 7.5 + thesis seminar 7.5 + science communication 5 + thesis 10 = 60. The ordinary minor is offered by another faculty or faculties. The first two named faculty alternatives, Climate Change, End Times, Sustainability and Religion, Space and Place, are selected neutrally; the optional module is not added. Retain the previously selected Cultural and Political Impact of Religion specialisation under its broad academic-identity basis, independently of UCR fit; Origins of Religion is an unselected alternative. Quranic Arabic 1 plus an optional module is a mutually exclusive alternative to the ordinary 15-EC minor, not extra credit. Article 7.1 separately permits abroad, education and spiritual-care options of up to 30 EC and Board-approved course replacements; these conditioned alternatives do not turn the ordinary 15-EC faculty requirement into unrestricted minor space. Applicable degree total, approval and progress rules remain. English instruction remains supported. Current academic-year cover/interior and adopted date establish applicability despite a stale cover running line and concept metadata. The current formal choice clauses were freshly retrieved and visually inspected on 2026-10-08.

routeSelection.basis: Retain the existing Cultural and Political Impact of Religion specialisation for its documented contemporary social/political emphasis, without reference to UCR fit. Mutually exclusive and Board-approved alternatives are not stacked.

programmes.label: Religious Studies at University of Groningen

exception.reason: A religion, cultural identity and political impact concept was tested against the selected broad specialisation. Several UCR courses illuminate religious myth, visual heritage, ancient identities, moral arguments and aspects of religious freedom or radicalisation. They do not supply a sustained inquiry into historical and lived Christianity, Judaism, Islam and South Asian traditions, religious experience and ritual, sacred texts and images, and religion-specific research methods. Replacing this 120-EC defining compulsory foundation with general political science, sociology, media analysis or psychology would leave the proposed curriculum centred on those general fields. The selected political-impact specialisation permits a focused related response, but it does not make incidental religious examples across unrelated courses a credible 24-course programme. Conflict/migration, environment, religious freedom, spiritual care and education directions were tested independently; none supplies the missing cumulative religion-centred study. This is an academic coherence decision, not a requirement to reproduce every external module or a professional qualification.
exception.curriculumContext: The corrected ordinary 180-EC Groningen pathway retains 120 EC compulsory first-/second-year religion study, a 15-EC university/personal minor, two selected 7.5-EC faculty choices, the Cultural and Political Impact of Religion specialisation, thesis seminar, 10-EC thesis and 5-EC science communication. The 15-EC minor is not enlarged into 30 EC unrestricted choice, and optional education/spiritual-care routes are not stacked.
exception.ucrCourseEvidence: Reviewed the current 151-row enriched UCR workbook, using names, descriptions, outline-derived profiles, disciplines, topics, methods, formal prerequisites and the six Fall 2026-start availability columns. The following concrete courses were assessed rather than assuming that a missing track label decides the outcome. MCCLITR211 World Myth & Literature studies ancient, Indian, Byzantine and Arabic narrative traditions and transmission across texts/images; it provides meaningful comparative myth study, not a World Religions survey or sacred-text hermeneutics sequence. MCCLITR112 Great Literary Works includes representations of organised religion, duty and memory but remains a broad Western literary survey. MCCHEAM112 Introduction to World Archaeology directly examines religious, social and gendered identities through ancient artefacts; MCCHEAM211 African Art & Heritage examines religious meaning in western-African visual traditions; MCCHEAM212 Renaissance Italy & Global Mediterranean includes Islamic courts and cross-cultural artistic exchange; MCCHEAM315 Heritage & Ancient Democracy studies Athenian democracy intertwined with myth and religion. These are valuable specific contributions to religious culture, not cumulative courses in the traditions or religion-study methodologies of the target. GOSPHIL111 Introduction to Western Philosophy includes god, meaning and central Western arguments; GOSPHIL214 Philosophy of Mind includes Buddhist accounts of self. GOSPHIL212 Ethics studies major moral theories and applied issues but is not comparative religious ethics. MCCHEAM212 and other rows without an enriched outline were assessed only at their documented description scope. No religious content was inferred from an attractive course title. GOSLAWJ111 Human Rights: Law & Philosophy explicitly includes Aquinas, natural law and rights in traditional societies and can inform religion/freedom questions. GOSPOLI313 Peace & Conflict covers ideological conflict, historical grievances and reconciliation; HCBPSYC315 Youth Resilience to Extremism conducts radicalisation-resilience research. Neither is relabelled as religion-specific violence or theology. GOSSOCI111/214/311 provide social theory, modernity, civil society and migrant inclusion; HCBPSYC111 examines social influences on beliefs and behaviour; GOSSOCI212 provides qualitative methods. These can support inquiry into religious communities but the documented content cannot be assumed to teach anthropology, sociology or psychology of religion. General media and communication courses can assist representation or science communication, but they do not establish a religion/media sequence. More general courses cannot be added solely to reach 24 courses or six advanced courses. Feasibility was assessed at the academic coherence gate before scheduling: no 24-course set was accepted, so no invented timetable or course credits are encoded. The ordinary selected route does not include Quranic Arabic, so the lack of Arabic is not a veto on its closest-match concept. The spiritual-care candidate would require an actual care/meaning curriculum, and the educational candidate an actual religion-teaching curriculum; general health psychology or rhetorical communication does not establish either. The selected climate/end-times and religion/space/place courses are not matched to general environmental policy merely because both discuss climate or place.

candidateAssessment.concept: Religious traditions, lived experience and cultural identity
candidateAssessment.assessment: The myth, religious heritage and philosophical material is meaningful but does not sustain the traditions, ritual, lived experience and religion-specific methods needed to organise a complete programme.

candidateAssessment.concept: Religion, migration, conflict and political freedom
candidateAssessment.assessment: Rights, extremism and conflict provide useful related content, while general political/social-theory additions do not supply an entire programme of the cultural and political impact of religion.
Environmental-justice and environmental-media courses lack the required comparative religion, end-times and sacred-space content; a general environmental curriculum would change the object of study.

candidateAssessment.concept: Religion, sexual health and spiritual care
candidateAssessment.assessment: Health psychology, lifespan psychology and ethics can support human care, but do not supply spiritual-care practice, religious meaning frameworks or a religion-and-care curriculum.
Communication and general youth-resilience research do not constitute religion-teaching knowledge, didactics or an educational practice sequence.
